To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combined effects of metals and PAHs can influence the structure of benthic food webs.

(i) the presence of metals in sediments influences the growth, reproduction, and survival of invertebrate benthic grazers and their predators; (ii) the presence of PAHs in sediments influences benthic microalgae, and the growth, reproduction and survival of inverterate benthic grazes and their predators; and (iii) the presence of both metals and PAHs in the sediments influence the growth, reproduction or survival of microalgae,
the combined effects of metals and PAHs can alter benthic foodwebs in a manner that is different from the individual effects of metals or PAHs alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How does a mixture of metals and PAHs influence the structure and function of benthic food webs?
how complex mixtures affect benthic communities, and how these communities are influenced by the interactions among the different components in the mixtures.
how contaminants alter energy flow through benthic food webs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of metals and PAHs are additive and synergistic, depending on the species and trophic level.
the interactive effects of metals and PAHs can be both positive and negative on benthic communities, and that these effects can be mediated by food web structure and interactions.
the interactive effects of PAHs and metals in sediments are complex, and that the nature of the interactions is influenced by a number of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that complex mixtures of metals (Cu, Pb, Zn, Cd, and Ni) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) can have interactive effects on benthic foodwebs.
metals and PAHs influence benthic food webs in a variety of ways that can lead to either positive or negative effects on the structure of the food web.
metals and PAHs can have additive and antagonistic effects on the structure of benthic food webs, and that these effects can change with time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of complex mixtures are more severe than those of individual compounds and that the effects of mixtures are often non-additive.
contaminants can influence the structure of benthic foodwebs by changing the relative abundance of different trophic groups and the interactions between them.
the effects of complex mixtures of chemicals on benthic communities are more complex than the effects of the individual contaminants.
